goal: Create a polished 90-second hackathon demo showing Atelier as an interactive AI architecture firm where GPT-6 Astra coordinates specialist work, observable tools, persistent design revisions and an explorable 3D result.
prompt: Create a fast, evidence-led 90-second product demo for Atelier. Open inside the real 3D office and establish the idea: the user enters an AI architecture firm instead of opening separate chatbots. Show the red visitor, key specialist rooms and a natural-language brief. Show GPT-6 Astra turning the brief into a dependency-aware task graph, differentiated specialists working concurrently, real Activity/tool events and saved revisions. Show project/design.json rendered by Three.js, then orbit, cutaway and Walk inside. Demonstrate contextual steering by selecting an exterior element and requesting a red finish while preserving unrelated work; show the revision only if it actually completes. Use the saved Yellow Aperture House browser, walkthrough, Blender, GLB and JSON evidence where helpful, but label it as an earlier GPT-5.6 Terra evidence run rather than Astra output. Do not fabricate workstation activity, review approval, steering completion or production readiness. End with: 'I hired an AI architecture firm—and walked into its office while the team was working.' and the Atelier URL.

narration.script: What if working with AI felt like entering a real architecture firm, instead of opening four separate chatbot windows? This is Atelier. The three-dimensional office is the interface, and every room represents real responsibility. I brief the firm naturally using text or voice. GPT-6 Astra structures the requirements and creates a dependency-aware task graph. The Architect develops space and structure while the Designer establishes the visual direction. Ready specialists work concurrently; dependent tasks consume their saved results, and the Critic reviews the combined design. This is real, observable work. Activity exposes task status, dependencies and tool events. Isolated E2B workstations can inspect files and use Blender, while validated proposals become persistent revisions instead of silently overwriting one another. The source of truth is machine-editable design JSON. Three.js turns it into an interactive model I can orbit, cut away and walk through. I can then select one exterior element and ask the Designer to make it red. Atelier preserves the unrelated geometry and furniture, reviews the update and records a new revision. The result includes canonical JSON, GLB, Blender source and rendered artifacts. Atelier combines agentic engineering, computer use and interactive three-dimensional design into one experience. I hired an AI architecture firm, and walked into its office while the team was working.
